reproduction_target: Computational reconstruction of a haplotype-resolved telomere-to-telomere genome of Indigofera pseudotinctoria and the analyses built on it: hifiasm/HiCanu/NextDenovo assembly with HapHiC Hi-C scaffolding and TGS-GapCloser/quarT2T gap closing; repeat, ncRNA and protein-coding annotation (LTR_retriever, RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker, Infernal, RNAmmer, tRNAscan-SE, BRAKER/Augustus/TSEBRA, GUSHR/GeMoMa); haplotype comparison (MUMmer4, GenomeSyn, SyRI, BEDTools); allele identification and allele-specific expression (JCVI, Diamond, GMAP, Nanopolish, HISAT2/StringTie, DESeq2, lme4); phylogenomics and WGD (OrthoFinder, MAFFT, Gblocks, RAxML-NG, PAML, CAFE, BLASTP/MCScanX, KaKs_Calculator); and transcriptome-metabolome integration (Analyst/MultiQuant processing, WGCNA, PlantTFDB, Cytoscape). Wet-lab work (DNA extraction, PacBio/ONT/Hi-C/RNA-seq library preparation and sequencing, metabolite extraction and UPLC-MS/MS acquisition) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis decomposition from the 'Materials and methods' subsections (Plant materials and DNA extraction; Library preparation and sequencing; Genome assembly (1)-(3); Genome annotation (1)-(3); Haplotype comparison and structural variation analysis; Identification of haplotype-specific and ASE genes; Identification of homeologous and orthologous gene sets; Phylogenetic analyses and gene family expansion/contraction; Screening for whole genome duplication events; UPLC-MS/MS detection; Transcriptional regulation of flavonoid biosynthesis). One extra C-step (C12) is added for the BUSCO/QV/LAI assembly evaluation that is reported in Results with no Methods description at all. The repository https://github.com/Jinghanpeng313/Indigofera-pseudotinctoria-T2T-genome was read at landing-page + README prose level only (no source line-by-line reading): 7 numbered module directories holding 33 .sh/.py/.R scripts, plus README.md; no lockfile, no container, no conda/renv environment file, no requirements file, no releases or tags at repository root. A step whose named tool is plainly covered by one of those scripts gets code=2; steps run in GUI/web tools or with no corresponding script (Juicebox, contaminant filtering, lme4 modelling, PlantTFDB, Cytoscape, Analyst/MultiQuant, CCS, Guppy) get code=1 (reconstructable from prose). Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: HiFi CCS read generation from PacBio Sequel II subreads using the CCS software (https://github.com/PacificBiosciences/ccs) with min passes = 3 and min RQ = 0.99 to yield >Q20 HiFi reads
ONT basecalling of PromethION FAST5 signal with the GPU Guppy basecaller v3.4.4 high-precision flip-flop model, retaining reads with Q > 7
Quality control of Hi-C and paired-end short reads ('the quality control measures were identical to those described above') - no tool, no thresholds, no command
Haplotype-resolved de novo assembly with hifiasm co-assembling PacBio HiFi, ONT ultra-long and Hi-C data in haplotype-resolved mode, producing Hap1 and Hap2 contig sets
Removal of contigs of non-nuclear origin (microbial or plastid contamination) - no tool, database or threshold named
Hi-C scaffolding of each haplotype independently with HapHiC to produce chromosome-scale assemblies
Manual correction of misjoins and inversions on Hi-C contact matrices visualised in Juicebox
Reassembly of ONT ultra-long and PacBio HiFi reads with HiCanu and NextDenovo to supply sequence for gap closing
Iterative gap filling with TGS-GapCloser and quarT2T, plus manual curation and read-remapping verification of gaps on chromosomes 1, 5 and 8
Telomere identification by screening for the plant telomeric repeat motif AAACCCT
Centromere identification with CentIER v2.0 and merging of the centromere sequences obtained by the two methods (the second method is not named)
Assembly quality evaluation reported in Results as BUSCO completeness, Merqury-style QV and LTR Assembly Index (LAI) - no tool, version, lineage dataset or command appears anywhere in Methods
LTR retrotransposon detection with LTR_harvest and LTR_FINDER, refined with LTR_retriever
De novo transposable-element prediction with RepeatModeler
Homology-based repeat annotation with RepeatMasker against the Dfam and RepBase databases
Repeat-library curation: protein-coding contamination filtering with ProtExcluder, deduplication with VSEARCH, classification with DeepTE
Tandem repeat detection with TRF and protein-level repeat detection with RepeatProteinMask
Small non-coding RNA detection with Infernal against Rfam using --rfam --cut_ga --nohmmonly
Ribosomal RNA prediction with RNAmmer using the eukaryotic model
tRNA identification with tRNAscan-SE in eukaryotic mode (-E -G)
Homology-based gene prediction with BRAKER using homologous peptide alignments from closely related species (species set not named)
RNA-seq alignment to the reference with HISAT2 followed by transcript assembly with StringTie for transcriptome-guided gene prediction
Ab initio gene prediction with Augustus trained on the StringTie transcript set
Integration of the three evidence tracks into a final gene set with TSEBRA
UTR and alternative-splicing definition with GUSHR and GeMoMa from RNA-seq alignments; longest transcript per locus retained, non-ORF regions designated UTR
Hap1 vs Hap2 synteny assessment with MUMmer4 and visualisation with GenomeSyn
Structural variation calling between haplotypes with SyRI
Distance between inversion regions and nearest transposable elements with BEDTools, with a null expectation from 100 random shuffles of inversion positions
Syntenic block identification and one-to-one allelic pair assignment with JCVI using --cscore=0.99
Homology assignment for non-syntenic genes with Diamond (E-value < 1e-5, identity > 80%, coverage > 80%) and GMAP coordinate overlap > 50%; identical-CDS and haplotype-specific gene classification
5mC methylation extraction from ONT reads with Nanopolish and TE/methylation distribution analysis with BEDTools
Mapping of six-tissue RNA-seq to the haplotype-resolved genome with HISAT2 and FPKM estimation with StringTie from uniquely mapped reads
Allele-specific expression testing with DESeq2 (fold change > 2, corrected P < 0.05)
Classification of ASE gene pairs into haplotype-dominant (Hap), sub/neo-functionalised (SubNeo) and NoDiff using the stated one-third-of-tissues rule
Allelic bias evaluation with a mixed-effects linear model from the R lme4 package, minor-allele contribution, and LOESS regression of total expression against allelic ratio
Orthologous group inference across I. pseudotinctoria and 16 sequenced species with OrthoFinder, longest-transcript extraction and removal of miscoded / prematurely terminated genes
Functional annotation and enrichment testing of species-specific genes against Gene Ontology and KEGG
Multiple alignment of single-copy ortholog coding sequences with MAFFT and removal of poorly aligned blocks with Gblocks
Maximum-likelihood species tree construction with RAxML-NG using 100 bootstrap replicates
Branch substitution-rate and species divergence-time estimation with PAML
Gene family expansion / contraction analysis with CAFE (birth-death model) on the OrthoFinder orthogroups
All-vs-all self-BLASTP of primary protein sequences followed by collinear block identification with MCScanX
Synonymous substitution rate (Ks) computation for syntenic gene pairs with KaKs_Calculator and WGD inference from the Ks distribution

Metabolomics peak detection, integration and quantification of MRM data with Analyst 1.6.3 and MultiQuant; missing-value imputation with 1/5 of each metabolite minimum and retention of metabolites with QC CV < 0.5

Weighted co-expression network construction with WGCNA blockwiseModules (soft threshold power = 16, TOMtype = signed, mergeCutHeight = 0.25, minModuleSize = 50) after filtering genes with TPM < 1 in all tissues
Transcription factor identification in the I. pseudotinctoria proteome with PlantTFDB using default parameters
Visualisation of the gene-TF interaction network in Cytoscape

Genomic DNA extraction from a single I. pseudotinctoria cv. 'Yudong' plant (Germplasm ID XKY20150201) by the SDS method with QIAGEN Genomic-tip purification, and DNA QC (agarose, NanoDrop One, Qubit 3.0 dsDNA HS)
PacBio HiFi SMRTbell library construction (SMRTbell Express Template Prep Kit 2.0, g-TUBE shearing to 15-18 kb, BluePippin >15 kb size selection) and sequencing on PacBio Sequel II
ONT library construction (NEBNext Ultra II End Repair/dA-tailing, BluePippin size selection, LSK109 ligation) and ultra-long sequencing on PromethION
Hi-C library construction from ~2 g fresh leaves (formalin fixation, crosslinking, nuclei suspension, digestion, ligation, end-repair, purification) and sequencing on MGI-2000
Six-tissue sampling and RNA-seq library construction and sequencing used for annotation, FPKM/ASE and co-expression analyses (library protocol and platform not described in Methods)

Metabolite extraction (50 mg freeze-dried tissue, 70% cold methanol, ultrasonication, 12,000 rpm centrifugation, 0.22 um filtration) and UPLC-MS/MS acquisition on ExionLC AD coupled to QTRAP 6500+ in MRM mode with the stated gradient, source and QC-injection settings

headline.static_readiness: 0/47 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/47 (0%) at the stage-1 ceiling. Every one of the 47 computational steps scores Data = 0, because the paper contains NO Data availability statement and NO accession of any kind (no NCBI BioProject/SRA, no ENA, no GSA/CNGB, no GEO, no figshare/Zenodo/Dryad) for the PacBio HiFi reads, ONT ultra-long reads, Hi-C reads, six-tissue RNA-seq, metabolomics tables, or for the two assembled haplotype genomes and their annotations. Axis-min is therefore 0 everywhere, giving NI (recoverable by author contact, not X) for all 47 steps and zero RI. The code axis is comparatively strong - 39 of 47 steps map to a named script in the public GitHub repository - so a data deposition alone would move a large fraction of these steps up; the version axis would still cap at 1 because the repository ships no lockfile, no container and no environment file, and the README pins only floating lower bounds (Python >= 3.8, R >= 4.1).
headline.coverage: 47 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the GitHub landing page and README prose; 6 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. Computational coverage = 47/53 = 88.7%. A Code availability statement is present and the repository resolves (HTTP 200, public, 50 commits, 7 module directories). No Data availability statement exists anywhere in the bioRxiv v1 full text.

gaps.where: All 47 computational steps; paper-level (no Data availability section anywhere in the bioRxiv v1 full text)
gaps.missing: No accession, BioProject, repository identifier, DOI or download URL is stated for ANY dataset. The full text contains a 'Code availability' section, an 'Author contributions' section, a 'Competing interests' section and an 'Acknowledgments' section, but no data statement of any kind - not even an 'available upon request' sentence. Absent: PacBio HiFi reads, ONT ultra-long FAST5/FASTQ, Hi-C reads, the six-tissue RNA-seq reads, the UPLC-MS/MS metabolite tables, and the two gap-free haplotype assemblies (647.38 Mb Hap1 and 657.52 Mb Hap2) with their annotations - the central deliverable of the paper. The 16 comparison species' protein sets used by OrthoFinder are described only as 'we downloaded their protein sequences' with no species list, assembly versions or sources.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw HiFi/ONT/Hi-C/RNA-seq reads under an INSDC BioProject (or GSA/CNGB) and the two haplotype assemblies plus GFF3 annotations under a versioned accession, restate the accessions in a Data availability section, and add a table listing each of the 16 comparison genomes with its assembly accession and version. This single change lifts the axis-min of all 47 steps off zero.

gaps.where: All 47 computational steps; repository root and Methods
gaps.missing: (gap 2a no-version + 2b floating-bound) Only three version-like designations appear in the entire Methods text: Guppy v3.4.4, CentIER v2.0 and Analyst 1.6.3 (plus the major-version tool names MUMmer4 and, in the repository, cafe5). The other ~40 named tools - hifiasm, HapHiC, HiCanu, NextDenovo, TGS-GapCloser, quarT2T, LTR_harvest, LTR_FINDER, LTR_retriever, RepeatModeler, RepeatMasker, ProtExcluder, VSEARCH, DeepTE, TRF, RepeatProteinMask, Infernal, RNAmmer, tRNAscan-SE, BRAKER, HISAT2, StringTie, Augustus, TSEBRA, GUSHR, GeMoMa, GenomeSyn, SyRI, BEDTools, JCVI, Diamond, GMAP, Nanopolish, DESeq2, lme4, OrthoFinder, MAFFT, Gblocks, RAxML-NG, PAML, CAFE, BLASTP, MCScanX, KaKs_Calculator, WGCNA, clusterProfiler, PlantTFDB, Cytoscape - carry a citation number and no version. The repository README's 'Computational Environment' section states only 'Python >= 3.8' and 'R >= 4.1' (floating lower bounds, gap 2b) and names no package at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi.lock (or a container image with a recorded digest) covering the assembly, annotation and comparative-genomics tool chain, plus an renv.lock for the R layer (DESeq2, lme4, WGCNA, clusterProfiler, ggplot2), and record the resolved interpreter versions. This is the only route to version = 2 and therefore the only route to R-star eligibility.

gaps.where: C15 (RepeatMasker with Dfam and RepBase), C18 (Infernal against Rfam), C37 (GO and KEGG), C46 (PlantTFDB)
gaps.missing: Every external reference database is named without a release identifier or download date: Dfam (no release), RepBase (no release; also a licence-gated resource since 2019), Rfam (no release), Gene Ontology and KEGG (URLs only), PlantTFDB (no version). Under the fetch-required taxonomy these cannot be classified A/B/C at stage 1 because that requires reading the workflow scripts; the prose alone pins nothing.
gaps.how_to_close: State the release string and download date of each database, and have the repository scripts fetch a versioned artifact (class A) rather than consume a user-supplied local path.

gaps.where: C3 (Hi-C / short-read QC), C5 (contaminant contig removal), C12 (BUSCO/QV/LAI evaluation), C21 (BRAKER protein evidence), C36 (16 comparison species)
gaps.missing: Five load-bearing procedures are referred to but never described. C3 is given only as 'the quality control measures were identical to those described above', and no earlier passage states a read-QC tool or threshold. C5 removes 'contigs showing non-nuclear origin (microbial or plastid contamination)' with no tool or database. C12 - the assembly quality claim that carries the T2T assertion (98% BUSCO, QV 71, LAI 20) - has no Methods paragraph at all: no BUSCO version or lineage dataset, no k-mer/QV tool, no LAI tool. C21 uses 'homologous peptide alignment from closely related species' without naming the species or the protein sets. C36 aligns 'protein sets collected from 16 sequenced species' without listing them.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Methods paragraph for read QC, decontamination and assembly evaluation naming each tool, version, database and threshold, and list the protein/genome sources by accession.

gaps.where: C28 (100x inversion-position shuffling null model), C39 (RAxML-NG with 100 bootstrap replicates)
gaps.missing: Both steps are stochastic and no random seed is stated in Methods; the substitution model for RAxML-NG is also not stated. Results from these steps are reproducible only distributionally.
gaps.how_to_close: State and consume an explicit seed in the shuffling script and in the RAxML-NG invocation, and record the substitution model.

gaps.where: C44 (metabolomics data processing with Analyst 1.6.3 and MultiQuant)
gaps.missing: Peak detection, integration and quantification of the MRM data depend on SCIEX's proprietary Analyst / MultiQuant software. The version is pinned for Analyst (1.6.3) but MultiQuant is unversioned, and neither is redistributable, so this step is capped at NI by the proprietary ceiling regardless of the other axes.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exported peak tables (and, if possible, the raw .wiff files) so that downstream quantification can be re-derived without the licensed software.

gaps.where: Repository modules 1-7 (all 33 scripts), inspected at landing-page level only
gaps.missing: The README states 'Each directory may contain multiple scripts. Please read the comments within individual scripts for detailed usage instructions.' There is no top-level driver, no workflow manager (no Snakemake/Nextflow/Make), no configuration file and no input manifest, so the execution order and the path/sample conventions live inside the scripts. Whether absolute paths or sample-specific constants are hardcoded cannot be settled at stage 1 - this gap is flagged as suspected, to be confirmed or dropped by a stage-2 code read.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a driver (Snakefile/Nextflow/Makefile) or a numbered run order plus a config file separating paths and sample identifiers from logic.

gaps.where: C35 (lme4 mixed model and LOESS), C46 (PlantTFDB), C47 (Cytoscape), C3, C5, C10, C12
gaps.missing: Seven steps have no corresponding script in the repository as far as the module listing shows: the allelic-bias mixed-effects model and LOESS regression, the TF identification, the network visualisation, the read QC, the decontamination, the telomere motif screen and the assembly evaluation. For C35 the model formula, random-effect structure and LOESS span are also absent from the prose, so the step is neither scripted nor specified.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the remaining analysis scripts, or state the model formulae and parameters in Methods so they are reconstructable.
